subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an energy store?
questions.explain: Electrical is a pathway by which energy is transferred, not a store; the recognised stores include kinetic, chemical and gravitational potential.

questions.q: Energy in a stretched spring is held in which energy store?
questions.explain: Stretching or compressing a spring stores energy in its elastic potential store.

questions.q: Which of these is a valid way in which energy can be transferred?
questions.explain: Energy can be transferred mechanically, electrically, by heating or by radiation; the others named are stores, not transfer pathways.

questions.q: The principle of conservation of energy states that energy:
options: Cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred between stores
Increases each time it is transferred
questions.explain: Energy is conserved: it can be transferred, stored or dissipated, but the total amount stays the same.

questions.q: Energy that is described as 'dissipated' has been:
options: Spread out to the surroundings, usually as thermal energy
questions.explain: Dissipated (wasted) energy is transferred to the thermal store of the surroundings and becomes less useful.

questions.q: Which equation correctly gives the efficiency of a device?
options: Useful output energy transfer / total input energy transfer
Total input energy transfer / useful output energy transfer
Useful output energy transfer x total input energy transfer
Total input energy transfer - useful output energy transfer
questions.explain: Efficiency = useful output energy transfer divided by total input energy transfer (equivalently using power).

questions.q: Which of the following is a renewable energy resource?
questions.explain: Wind is renewable because it is replenished naturally, whereas coal, gas and nuclear fuels are finite.

questions.q: The three fossil fuels are:
questions.explain: Fossil fuels are coal, oil and natural gas, formed from the remains of dead organisms over millions of years.

questions.q: For a pendulum swinging freely, at the highest point of its swing most of its energy is in the:
questions.explain: At the highest point the pendulum is momentarily at rest and raised, so energy is mainly in the gravitational potential store.

questions.q: A ball falls from a height with negligible air resistance. The main energy transfer is from:
options: Gravitational potential store to kinetic store
Kinetic store to gravitational potential store
Elastic potential store to kinetic store
questions.explain: As the ball falls it loses height and gains speed, so gravitational potential energy is transferred to the kinetic store.

questions.q: When a moving car brakes and slows down, friction transfers energy mainly to the:
options: Thermal store of the brakes and surroundings
Elastic potential store of the tyres
Gravitational potential store of the car
questions.explain: Friction in the brakes dissipates the kinetic energy to the thermal store, warming the brakes and surroundings.

questions.q: Why can no real device ever be 100% efficient?
options: Some energy is always dissipated to less useful stores such as thermal energy
Energy is destroyed inside the device
Useful output is always greater than input
Machines create extra energy as heat
questions.explain: Real devices always waste some energy, usually to the thermal store, so useful output is less than total input.

questions.q: Which is a genuine disadvantage of using wind turbines to generate electricity?
options: Output is unreliable because it depends on the weather
They release large amounts of carbon dioxide when running
They use up a finite fuel supply
They cannot be built on land
questions.explain: Wind is intermittent, so turbines cannot guarantee a constant supply, unlike a controllable fossil-fuel power station.

questions.q: Increasing the use of renewable resources instead of fossil fuels helps mainly by:
options: Reducing carbon dioxide emissions and conserving finite reserves
Guaranteeing a constant supply in all weather
questions.explain: Renewables emit little or no CO2 during generation and do not deplete finite fossil-fuel reserves.

questions.q: In a closed system, the total energy:
options: Stays the same, even though it moves between stores
questions.explain: A closed system has no net energy transfer in or out, so the total energy is constant even as it moves between stores.

questions.q: A 2 kg object moves at 3 m/s. Using kinetic energy = 1/2 x m x v squared, its kinetic energy is:
questions.explain: KE = 1/2 x 2 x 3 squared = 1/2 x 2 x 9 = 9 J.

questions.q: A 5 kg mass is lifted 2 m. Taking gravitational field strength g = 10 N/kg, the gain in gravitational potential energy is:
questions.explain: GPE = m x g x h = 5 x 10 x 2 = 100 J.

questions.q: A device is supplied with 200 J and transfers 50 J usefully. Its efficiency is:
A motor has an input power of 100 W and a useful output power of 80 W. Its efficiency is:
questions.explain: Efficiency = useful output power / total input power = 80 / 100 = 0.80 = 80%.

questions.q: Which resource is non-renewable but produces no carbon dioxide during electricity generation?
questions.explain: Nuclear fuel is finite (non-renewable) but the fission process releases no carbon dioxide when generating electricity.
